# ng-point

> Dev-mode-only Angular package: Alt+Click any element in your running app to capture an LLM-ready context block — component name, file:line, template, cleaned HTML, directives, parent — copied to your clipboard with an optional instruction, ready to paste into an AI coding agent. Published as @abiramcodes/ng-point. Works with Angular 21 and 22. MIT licensed.

ng-point runs only in development builds — production builds constant-fold it away and never load it. Secrets (JWTs, API keys, tokens) are redacted at capture, before anything reaches the clipboard. There is no build plugin and no server: the overlay is a non-modal `<dialog>` and source locations come from Angular's own dev-mode compiler metadata.

## Install

npm: `npm install -D @abiramcodes/ng-point`
pnpm: `pnpm add -D @abiramcodes/ng-point`

## Setup

```ts
// app.config.ts
import { provideNgPoint } from '@abiramcodes/ng-point';

export const appConfig: ApplicationConfig = {
  providers: [provideRouter(routes), provideNgPoint()],
};
```

Alt+Click any element (macOS: Option+Click) → review the context block → type an optional instruction → Enter copies and queues. Alt+Shift+Click adds more elements (up to 5 per session). Alt+arrows retarget to the parent/child element. Esc discards. Per-element opt-out: the `ngPointIgnore` directive. Kill-switch: `localStorage.ngPointDisabled = '1'`.

## Configuration highlights

```ts
provideNgPoint({
  activationModifier: 'alt' | 'ctrl-shift',
  maxSelections: 5,
  maxQueueEntries: 6,
  sensitiveSelectors: ['input[autocomplete="cc-number"]'],
  extraRedactionPatterns: [/TICKET-\d+/],
  includeTemplateLine: true,
  resolveFilePath: (filePath, element) => `remotes/checkout/${filePath}`,
})
```

All fields optional; these are the defaults.

## Agent skill

ng-point ships a skill file so coding agents can set it up and drive it without
being told how. It lives in the repo's `skills/ng-point/` folder; install it from
skills.sh — the open skills registry:

    npx skills add abiramcodes/ng-point

The CLI detects the agent (OpenCode, Claude Code, Cursor, and 75+ more) and
installs into the folder that agent scans. Without npx, fetch the file directly:

    mkdir -p .agents/skills/ng-point \
      && curl -fsSL \
      https://raw.githubusercontent.com/abiramcodes/ng-point/main/skills/ng-point/SKILL.md \
      -o .agents/skills/ng-point/SKILL.md

Claude Code reads `.claude/skills/ng-point/` instead — same command, that folder.

## Facts for agents

- License: MIT. Author: Abiram (https://www.abikb.xyz/).
- Zero runtime footprint: install as a devDependency; production bundles never load it.
- No zone APIs; works zone-based or zoneless Angular.
- Angular 21 and 22 (`@angular/core`/`@angular/common` `^21.0.0 || ^22.0.0`); the optional `Template:` line needs an app compiler of 22.1.4+.
- Clipboard-first: nothing is ever pushed into an agent session — the user copies and pastes.
- Output format is a compact, LLM-friendly block; multiple selections are joined by `---`.
